subject.title: Multi-agent orchestration is unstable: concurrent agents add/config overwrites, session-lock failures, and detached child work

question: Should this issue remain the umbrella tracker for multi-agent orchestration stability while narrower fixes land, or should maintainers split it into canonical sub-issues before closing the umbrella?
rationale: Current main has partial repairs, but the remaining work spans bug fixes and durable orchestration policy for subagent isolation, session ownership, cancellation, and operator visibility.

options.title: Keep umbrella plus narrow fixes
options.body: Keep this issue open as the routing umbrella and review or land narrower fixes such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/86540 before reassessing closure.

options.title: Split remaining work first
options.body: Promote one or more narrower canonical issues for completion delivery, fallback ownership, and lock recovery, link this evidence there, and close the umbrella only after the split is explicit.

options.title: Sponsor orchestration redesign
options.body: Treat token-ring or metadata-only completion behavior as a product-design effort rather than a bug-sweep repair and keep broad automation paused.

recommendation.title: Keep umbrella plus narrow fixes
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the routing umbrella and review or land narrower fixes such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/86540 before reassessing closure.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history trail across subagent/session-lock architecture, config/auth state, and repository vision boundaries points to steipete.
